_README: Every number in this file was MEASURED by running the command recorded beside it.
Nothing here is illustrative, and nothing here is computed by the API at request
time — GET /api/proofs serves these as RECORDED measurements and labels them as
such. The two facts that endpoint reports live (the crash-window count and whether
the vector index is still in the plan) are computed in axiom/api.py, not read from
To refresh a block: run its `command`, paste the numbers, update `measured_at`.
`in_use` on a tool entry is the fact, not a guess parsed out of the status prose:
true means it is part of the running deployed system TODAY. Bedrock's models ARE
enabled on the deployment account and both of them answer, but the on-demand quota
for Titan V2 is 0.0 requests per minute and is not adjustable, so nothing can call
it in a loop; the CloudFront distribution serves no traffic. Both are false, and a
footer that counts them as in use is the exact species of overclaim this project
The file lives beside the code rather than in docs/ because vercel.json's
excludeFiles trims docs/ and scripts/ out of the deployed function bundle.

chaos.where: CockroachDB Cloud v26.2.5, cluster axiom-memory (BASIC, AWS us-east-1), AXIOM_OFFLINE=1
chaos.also: 33 kills / 5 replays / 0 duplicates / 62.4s on an isolated single local node v26.2.3 — the result does not depend on the topology

scale.claim: Claim cost tracks OUTSTANDING work, not total work ever done: finished tasks leave the partial claim index. Scoped honestly — this is a statement about the INDEX, not about distributed throughput.

stripe.command: POST /api/proof/stripe on https://axiom-one-sage.vercel.app, then the refund re-sent by hand from a plain terminal: curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/refunds -u sk_test_…: -H 'Idempotency-Key: axm_bb4799e8afaed374341e70936556850c6d221e63b52d599f' -d charge=ch_3U4A9yAwRnm0fQgO0yMnQJJz -d amount=30000 -d 'metadata[axiom_order_ref]=AXM-PROOF-4030f815'
stripe.where: Stripe test mode (livemode: false), API version 2026-07-29.dahlia, against the live Vercel deployment
stripe.claim: Two Stripe calls, one refund. The second call came from a different machine with nothing but the idempotency key AXIOM had committed to CockroachDB BEFORE the crash, and Stripe returned the FIRST refund rather than creating a second — reporting idempotent-replayed: true and naming the earlier call in original-request: req_8j6Q6lmQ5Y3ccx. The key alone was sufficient.
stripe.verify: receipt_url is Stripe's own hosted receipt page and needs no Stripe login; GET /stripe-receipt on the deployment redirects to it. dashboard_url resolves only for the sandbox owner.
stripe.caveat: Stripe mints a fresh receipt_url token each time the charge is retrieved; the recorded token was checked to still return HTTP 200 unauthenticated on 2026-08-13. Idempotency keys expire at Stripe after 24 hours, so re-running the curl above today creates a SECOND refund instead of replaying — the replay evidence is this recorded run, not a repeatable command.

counterexample.where: same crash instant (W4), same provider database, one order, both agents
counterexample.claim: A fair transcript-memory baseline, killed at the same instant against the same provider, pays $600 for one $300 order. AXIOM pays $300.

cockroach_tools.name: Distributed Vector Indexing
cockroach_tools.detail: Two C-SPANN indexes on axiom_memory.embedding: axiom_memory_ann_by_context (four prefix columns, the recovery path) and axiom_memory_ann_by_tenant (broad recall). vector_cosine_ops written explicitly — omitting the opclass silently gives L2 and a <=> query then full-scans. Index use is asserted from EXPLAIN at request time, not assumed.

cockroach_tools.name: Cloud Managed MCP Server
cockroach_tools.status: In use, verified against the live server
cockroach_tools.detail: axiom/audit_mcp.py speaks to https://cockroachlabs.cloud/mcp over streamable HTTP with a scoped service-account key, discovering each tool's arguments from tools/list. Verified end to end: it correctly answers "was any order ever refunded twice?" with the BASELINE agent's duplicates and none of AXIOM's. Containment is three layers: a SELECT-only role, a single-statement guard, and default_transaction_read_only.

cockroach_tools.name: ccloud CLI
cockroach_tools.detail: The cluster the measured results ran on (axiom-memory, BASIC, AWS us-east-1, v26.2.5) is administered entirely through ccloud; scripts/provision_ccloud.sh wraps provisioning plus all three migrations.

cockroach_tools.name: Agent Skills Repo
cockroach_tools.status: Skill written, validated against the upstream validator, and SUBMITTED upstream — PR open, not merged
cockroach_tools.detail: skills/cockroachdb-application-development/implementing-crash-safe-work-queues/ passes cockroachlabs/cockroachdb-skills' own validate-spec.py --strict with zero errors and zero warnings, verified against upstream main at e14e86d. Submitted as https://github.com/cockroachlabs/cockroachdb-skills/pull/23 (607 insertions, two files, mergeable). It stays in_use: false on purpose — this file's rule is that in_use means part of the RUNNING DEPLOYED SYSTEM today, and an unmerged pull request to somebody else's repository is not that, however much it would flatter the count to say otherwise.

aws_services.name: AWS Lambda
aws_services.status: Deployed, public, and serving the demo
aws_services.detail: axiom-api (FastAPI behind Mangum) and axiom-worker, both us-east-2, arm64, python3.13. Measured on the real deployment: cold start INIT 1447-2258 ms, warm /api/health 169 ms, /api/crash-windows 2.7 ms, peak 149 MB of 512. The function's own URL is still 403 to anonymous callers at the account level; see API Gateway below, and the controlled experiment in README.md.

aws_services.name: Amazon API Gateway (HTTP API)
aws_services.status: In use — the public AWS front door
aws_services.detail: https://nq0i2ob395.execute-api.us-east-2.amazonaws.com — $default route, AWS_PROXY payload 2.0, 20 req/s burst 40. uptime_check.sh passes 6/6 against it. Reproducible via deploy/lambda/apigateway.sh (--destroy tears it down). NOT free here, and this line said '$0.00/month: HTTP APIs are 1M requests/month free through Aug 2027' until 2026-08-14 — which contradicted this file's own cost block. The 1M allowance is a TWELVE-MONTH offer and this account has none (accountPlanType PAID, 12 free-tier entries, all 'Always Free', zero '12 Months Free'), so requests bill at $1.00/M from the first one. Nothing bills at rest: API Gateway is per-request, so an idle HTTP API still costs nothing.
aws_services.why_it_works: A Function URL needs lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl for an ANONYMOUS principal, evaluated by the Function URL front end — that is what this account withholds. API Gateway needs lambda:InvokeFunction for the NAMED service principal apigateway.amazonaws.com, evaluated by the Lambda control plane, and it is honored normally. Both doors are live on the same function right now, which makes the account restriction a demonstration rather than an assertion: Function URL 403, HTTP API 200, same function, same moment.

aws_services.name: Amazon Bedrock
aws_services.status: Reachable and verified; NOT USABLE on this account — quota is structurally zero
aws_services.detail: amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 returns the 1024-dimension embedding the schema's VECTOR(1024) pins, and anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5 answers — both confirmed live from this account. Neither can be used, and the reason is worth stating precisely because a single successful probe looks like proof that it works.
aws_services.why_not_batch: Bedrock batch inference IS available on this account (100,000 records per job), and it has a MINIMUM of 100 records per job. The real memory corpus is 10 distinct seed texts. Padding a batch job with filler to clear that minimum would buy a checkbox by embedding meaningless strings, which is the species of overclaim this project exists to argue against — so it was not done.
aws_services.consequence: Embeddings are produced by the deterministic local stand-in (offline-blake2b-sketch-v1), and every axiom_memory row now SAYS so in embedding_model. The vector index, the C-SPANN prefix quarantine and the in-transaction recall are all real CockroachDB mechanics either way — what is not real is the claim that Bedrock produced the vectors, and that claim has been removed.

aws_services.name: CloudFront
aws_services.detail: Created during the fallback attempt at a public front door, before API Gateway solved it. It costs nothing and is now redundant.

aws_services.name: ECS Fargate / ALB / S3
aws_services.detail: Dockerfile and deploy/terraform/{ecs,alb,network,iam,logs}.tf exist. No cluster, service or task definition has been created — every one of those bills per hour rather than per request.

aws_services.name: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler
aws_services.status: In use — keeps the demo alive across four unattended weeks
aws_services.detail: Schedule axiom-worker-sweep, rate(5 minutes), ENABLED, target axiom-worker with {"mode":"drain","seconds":45,"idle_exit":true}. Verified firing: three separate invocations observed at 18:18, 18:23 and 18:24 local. This is what makes the board self-heal — judging runs Aug 19 to Sep 15 with nobody watching, and a queue that stalls on day three is a dead demo for the remaining four weeks. mode=drain, NOT chaos: the sweeper's job is to keep the demo healthy, and a background process that deliberately kills itself would make the error alarm meaningless. Chaos stays where a human triggers it.

aws_services.name: Amazon CloudWatch
aws_services.status: In use — 5 alarms, 1 dashboard, and it has already paged a human
aws_services.detail: axiom-api-errors, axiom-api-throttles, axiom-http-5xx, axiom-worker-errors, axiom-worker-silent, plus a dashboard. Thresholds are deliberately loose enough to survive AXIOM's own design: the demo crashes its worker ON PURPOSE at crash window W4, so axiom-worker-errors needs >30 errors in 15 minutes twice rather than >0, or every judge pressing RUN MISSION would page the owner. Proven end to end rather than assumed — an alarm was driven into ALARM state deliberately and the email arrived; its own history reads 'test complete, restored by observability.sh'. Always Free: 10 alarms, 1M requests, 5GB logs.

aws_services.name: Amazon SNS
aws_services.status: In use — alarm delivery; subscription PENDING until the owner clicks confirm
aws_services.detail: Topic axiom-ops-alerts, email subscription to the account owner. Always Free: 1,000 notifications/month, far beyond what five alarms will emit. NOTE the subscription reads PendingConfirmation until the confirmation email is clicked, and re-running observability.sh replaces a confirmed subscription with a pending one — that is a defect in the script, not in SNS, and it silently disarms alerting.

aws_services.name: AWS X-Ray
aws_services.status: In use — the crash-and-recovery path as a clickable trace
aws_services.detail: Active tracing on axiom-worker ONLY; axiom-api is deliberately PassThrough. An earlier revision of this entry said both, which was false — checked with aws lambda get-function-configuration and corrected. The distinction is not pedantry: an Active API behind a browser tab that polls would record a trace per poll and cost ~$1.73/month per open tab, over the $1.00 budget on one tab alone, while the worker's ~8,640 scheduled invocations a month cost about four cents. PassThrough means the API traces only when something upstream already decided to, and API Gateway tracing is off, so it records nothing. VERIFIED BY READING A REAL TRACE rather than by trusting the instrumentation: trace 1-6a7fb524-4be35a4b20bb6f981abc4b6a carries axiom.PREPARE, axiom.dispatch and axiom.SETTLE subsegments under an axiom.drain span, with these annotations actually present — PREPARE: prepare_outcome ('receipt' or 'parked_on_approval'), idempotency_key, amount_cents, task_id; dispatch: crash_window ('W4'), provider_status, idempotency_key; SETTLE: attempt_state, task_state, idempotency_key, task_id. Annotations are filterable in the console, so a judge can query crash_window = W4 and land on the exact instant this project is about — the provider has committed and AXIOM does not yet know — instead of reading a paragraph claiming it happens. The same trace shows three refunds over the $200 ceiling with prepare_outcome = parked_on_approval, which is the policy engine visible as telemetry. Sampling bounded at 5% plus a 1/sec reservoir. BILLED on this account at $5.00 per million traces recorded; realistic judging volume is a few thousand traces, so cents.

measured.command: aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name axiom-api --query TracingConfig.Mode ; aws xray batch-get-traces --trace-ids 1-6a7fb524-4be35a4b20bb6f981abc4b6a

aws_services.name: Amazon SES
aws_services.status: Sender verified, sending confirmed — wiring into the broadcast domain
aws_services.detail: Sender identity verified and a real send confirmed to Amazon's mailbox simulator (MessageId 010f01a0028ad822-005d6883-ca07-4c68-8189-afd522fbc98d-000000), which needs no recipient verification and touches no real inbox. Sandbox: 200 messages/day. SES is one of the twelve Always Free entries on this account. in_use stays false until the broadcast domain actually dispatches through it — the second worked example still uses the simulated relay today.

aws_services.name: Amazon Comprehend
aws_services.status: Wired into triage behind an authority boundary, OFF by default, and NOT free here
aws_services.detail: axiom/comprehend.py runs DetectKeyPhrases + DetectEntities + DetectSentiment over an exception description and may only NARROW what the rule table proposed: it can move an action toward escalate, never toward acting; it cannot move amount_cents at all (lowering $300 to $150 is self-authorization wearing a helpful face); it cannot raise its own confidence. assert_cannot_widen() enforces it and deliberately does not catch — an operational failure is absorbed a layer lower, so anything that escapes is a defect, and a defect that widens authority should fail the task. in_use is false because AXIOM_COMPREHEND is unset on both Vercel and Lambda, so it bills nothing while judges use the demo. BILLED on this account. accountPlanType is PAID with $0.00 remaining credits and twelve 'Always Free' entries and ZERO '12 Months Free' entries — so every free tier that is a twelve-month offer has expired here. Verified: aws freetier get-account-plan-state / get-free-tier-usage. $0.0001/unit; ~$0.09 spent on measurement.

measured.agreement_with_rule_table: 9 of 16 texts carrying a ground-truth kind; rules correct 15/16, Comprehend correct 10/16, Comprehend silent 6/16
measured.why_it_earns_its_place: llm._KIND_RULES is first-match-wins with late_delivery ABOVE fraud_suspected, so 'delivery delayed nine days and an unauthorized charge appeared on the stolen card' at $150 triages as an unattended refund under the $200 ceiling. A/B against the real engine: AXIOM_COMPREHEND=0 settles and moves the money; =1 escalates, 0 receipts minted. Comprehend found a real ordering bug in the rule table.

tests.detail: 44 risk, 36 resilience, 24 adapter, 22 proof, 18 second-domain, 17 invariant, 15 Lambda-worker, 14 schema-sync, 13 crash-window, 5 recall-plan
tests.caveat: 208 collected, 208 pass, 0 fail. This number is RECORDED, not computed at request time — a serverless function cannot run pytest — so it drifts the moment anyone adds a test. Re-run the command and update it in the same commit that adds one.

embedding_provenance.how_classified: By MEASUREMENT, not by assumption. A row is the offline sketch if cos(stored, offline_embed(its own content)) > 0.99999; it is the test fixture if it reproduces sin(r*0.7 + d*0.013) to 1e-6. Zero rows matched neither, and the relabel refused to run if any had.
embedding_provenance.what_was_wrong: axiom_memory.embedding_model was declared NOT NULL DEFAULT 'amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0' and no insert path ever set it, so every row claimed to hold a Titan V2 embedding while holding a blake2b sketch or a sine fixture. Nothing computed a wrong answer — both sides of every cosine comparison were the same embedder — but the table was stating something untrue about itself.
embedding_provenance.fix: axiom/memory.py writes embeddings.MODEL_ID explicitly; db/005_embedding_space.sql drops the default so forgetting it is an error rather than a lie; scripts/reembed.py moves the corpus if the embedder ever changes.
embedding_provenance.note: The 2,500 sine-fixture rows are tests/test_recall_plan.py's corpus, left on the demo cluster. They are in their own tenant and are what makes 'the vector index is still chosen at 2,500 rows' checkable on the live cluster rather than only locally.
embedding_provenance.corpus_size_moves: 2,511 at the moment of the relabel, and it will not read exactly that later. Every POST /api/proof/* run works in a tenant of its own and deletes it afterwards, so the row count breathes by a few dozen while a proof is in flight — an earlier read during one said 2,541. What is invariant, and what the relabel actually asserts, is that ZERO rows are unlabelled and zero matched neither embedder.

cost.account_plan: PAID · $0.00 remaining credits · 12 'Always Free' entries · 0 '12 Months Free'
cost.correction: Earlier revisions of this repository claimed '$0.00/month'. That was true of the services in use at the time and is NOT true now: API Gateway, X-Ray and Comprehend have no free-tier entry on this account because their free tiers are twelve-month offers and this account is past that window. The honest number is cents, not zero, and a project that argues for precise measurement does not get to round its own bill down to a rounder number.
cost.projection_through_judging: Under $1.00 through Sep 15 at realistic judging volume. API Gateway $1.00/M requests, X-Ray $5.00/M traces recorded, Comprehend off in production.
cost.guard: AWS Budget axiom-zero-spend at $1.00 with notifications at 1%, 50% and 100% — so the owner is emailed at $0.01 before anything meaningful accrues.

tests_note: 260 passed, 3 skipped, measured with AWS_* unset entirely — the suite is hermetic and needs no credentials, which is what makes it worth running. Was 208 before the Comprehend, SES and tracing suites landed. The 3 skips are live-AWS tests gated behind an explicit opt-in: ambient credentials are not consent to spend.
